name: Palais du Luxembourg
note: The Senate. Placed on OSM relation 975955's box turned 2° to its axes (centre and size measured off the relation with osmium, 2026-10-29); the relation and its ~90 building:parts are replaced. Garden front (−z) to the south: Gisors' gallery, the clock frontispiece under its square dome, the corner pavilions; the Rue de Vaugirard (+z): the domed gatehouse in its screen between the tall-roofed pavilions.

name: Fontaine Médicis
note: OSM node 782601793 and its basin (way 62848427, the garden's fence way 837832921 round it): centred on the basin, whose axis runs at bearing 92/272; the grotto front at the east end facing down the basin toward the palace (−z, bearing 272). The water is the city's own; the model draws the kerb, the urns and the fountain.

name: Musée du Luxembourg
note: The 1886 stone front on the Rue de Vaugirard (pilasters, brick centre, the door's segmental pediment, the sculpted pediment) and the trellised gallery behind it (owner's photographs, 2026-11-03): palaces/luxembourg-museum.ts. Placed on OSM way 170226810's box, front (−z) at bearing ~3.

name: Hôtel des Invalides
note: Placed on OSM relation 1463538's box turned 4° to its axes (measured with osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the Esplanade (bearing 4); the relation's building:part relations and Saint-Louis-des-Invalides (way 64955027, with its five parts) are replaced. The Église du Dôme (way 112452790 and its parts) is NOT claimed: it stays as OSM maps it under `invalidesDome`, in the notch the plan leaves empty at the south. The moat parapet and the batterie triomphale stand ~12 m in front of the footprint, on the esplanade.

name: Palais Bourbon — cour d'honneur gate
note: The entrance on the Place du Palais-Bourbon: the Corinthian colonnade on its steps between the two pavilions. Placed on the box of the five OSM building:parts it replaces (measured with osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the place, bearing 188.5.

name: Palais Bourbon — ranges and cour d'honneur
note: The Assemblée's wings round the Cour d'honneur and the western block's ranges round their courts (relation 19981961 and building:parts of relation 1019368, outlines from osmium on the Île-de-France extract, 2026-11-03; heights from IGN's lidar MNS: ranges 15–16.5 m to the copper leads, the SW pavilion 19 m). Drawn as three storeys of bays, balustrade, slate mansard with dormers and green copper on top; the court holds the cobbles, the round lawn with the granite sphere, the curved plaque wall, the two flower-bordered lawns with pyramid yews, and the lamps. The palace core, hemicycle, portico (`assembleePortico`) and gate (`bourbonGate`) stay as they were.

name: Palais Bourbon
note: The Assemblée nationale's palace round its courts: OSM maps it in 3D as ~45 building:parts (heights and roof shapes, the hemicycle's dome among them), so the massing is OSM's and this gives it the stone dress; the court gate is `bourbonGate` and the Seine portico `assembleePortico` (paris.json). No height, levels or roof here: they would flatten the parts' own (styleOnly drops them for parts anyway).

name: Hôtel de Lassay
note: The residence of the Assemblée's president beside the Palais Bourbon (1722–28, raised a storey in the 1840s): two storeys of tall windows in stone under a balustrade.

name: Palais de l'Élysée
note: The President's palace. Placed on OSM relation 1060803's box turned 26° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), its plan and courts extruded; −z (bearing 26) is the Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honoré with the portal, +z the gardens. (The brief's 'Hôtel d'Évreux relation/542353' is a different Hôtel d'Évreux — no. 19 Place Vendôme — and is not touched.)

name: Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances (Bercy)
note: The Bâtiment Colbert (OSM way 217512456 and its parts; the wedge pavilion 1227184965 and the helipad's circle 1227184966 inside its outline). Placed on the slab's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the footprint stopping at the quai so the river bed under its foot does not set its base: the model's river tower reaches 26 m beyond the footprint (−x, south-west) on round piers at the water, and its far pylon 11 m beyond it at the Rue de Bercy (+x). Rebuilt 2026-11-03 from IGN lidar, the orthophoto and photographs: docs/landmarks/MODEL-BERCY.md. Height 44 is the helipad's deck over a 38 m roof.

name: Palais Brongniart
note: The old Bourse: the Corinthian peristyle on its podium, steps at both ends, Cavel's wings making the cross. Placed on OSM way 54657155's box turned 17.5° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29).

name: Palais de la Légion d'Honneur
note: The Hôtel de Salm: the rotunda on the Quai Anatole-France (−z, bearing 26), the triumphal gate and colonnaded court on the Rue de Lille (+z). OSM relation 1002192's plan and court extruded, placed on its box turned 26° (osmium, 2026-10-29).

name: Palais de Tokyo — the parvis
note: Standalone in the court between the two wings (OSM ways 79219351 and 79219308, which stay, dressed below): the peristyle of square columns standing free before both inner faces and across the head of the court, roofed back to the walls (the 26 column parts, ways 1214526961–986, and the portico roof, way 79219265, are claimed: the model draws every one of them), the portico on the Avenue du Président-Wilson slant, the terraces down toward the Seine (+z, bearing 162) with the pool. The builder draws in plain metres; `size` is only the world-square box inscribed in the court round this point (±10 m E–W, ±26 m N–S: the nonbuildings audit measures a standalone entry by its unrotated box, and the court runs 18° off the meridian). Its terraces read the ground (Fit.groundAt): the court falls toward the river.

name: Hôtel de Matignon
note: The Prime Minister's hôtel on the Rue de Varenne, between its court and its garden: stone, slate.

name: Ministère des Affaires étrangères — Quai d'Orsay
note: Lacornée's Second Empire palace of the ministry on the Quai d'Orsay: batch6/fronts.ts, the restyle's three storeys under a mansard made an apartment block of it (Batch 6, 2026-10-31).

name: Hôtel de Toulouse (Banque de France)
note: Replaces the `classical` restyle on the same relation. Way 54046037 (named Hôtel de Toulouse in OSM) is the relation's outer ring, so one footprint. Placed on its box turned to the Rue Croix-des-Petits-Champs (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 110. The long elevation and the door at no. 39 from Commons "Façade principale BDF" and "Façade de la Banque de France, angle de la rue Baillif et de la rue Croix-des-Petits-Champs"; the other fronts unchecked. Mansart's hôtel and the Galerie Dorée are inside the block and not drawn.

name: Théâtre de l'Odéon
note: Peyre and de Wailly's theatre on the Place de l'Odéon. Placed on OSM way 338641511's box turned 1.5° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the place, bearing 358.5; the outline and its ~50 building:parts (the sixteen portico columns, their bases, the steps, the string courses, the roofs) are replaced. The eight-column Doric portico two deep, the arcades down both flanks, the hall's hipped roof and the stage house, where OSM's 3D maps them.

name: Théâtre du Châtelet
note: Davioud's west theatre on the Place du Châtelet. Placed on OSM way 53574718's box turned to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the place, bearing 112.5; the outline and its building:parts (the block, the auditorium's round-hipped roof, the lantern's posts) are replaced — paris.json's restyle of the pair is overridden by this replace. Arcaded porch, terrace and five-window loggia, the attic with its allegories, the arcaded flanks, the slate roofs and the auditorium's roof and lantern rising out of them.

name: Théâtre de la Ville
note: Davioud's east theatre on the Place du Châtelet, the Châtelet's twin facing it across the fountain. Placed on OSM way 53582122's box turned to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the place, bearing 292.5; outline and parts replaced (overriding paris.json's restyle of the pair).

name: Opéra-Comique (Salle Favart)
note: Bernier's Salle Favart. Placed on OSM way 54572719's box turned 15.5° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the Place Boieldieu, bearing 195.5: the perron, the three arched doorways, the great windows between paired Corinthian columns, the attic of windows and caryatids, the statues in the side niches, the mansard and the stage house.

name: Tribunal de commerce de Paris
note: Bailly's Tribunal de commerce on the Île de la Cité. Placed on OSM way 53601032's box turned 22.3° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), +z to the Quai de la Corse (bearing 22.3), −x the Boulevard du Palais; the block, its mansard part (relation 17416175), the court's glass roof and the dome's five parts are replaced. The dome stands off-centre where OSM maps it (x −9.5), on the Boulevard de Sébastopol's axis: square base, octagonal drum with paired columns, eight-sided ribbed dome, lantern, 45 m.

name: Observatoire de Paris
note: Perrault's Observatoire with its 1830s wings (OSM way 79611305, the whole range), square to the meridian: +z is the north front at the end of the Avenue de l'Observatoire with its square tower, −z the south front with the two octagonal towers; the Arago dome on the east tower, the wings' round towers and little domes at x ±44 (osmium, 2026-10-29).

name: Fontaine de l'Observatoire
note: The Fontaine des Quatre-Parties-du-Monde (OSM node 1248594605), centred on Carpeaux's group in its basin (OSM relation 1004052, the water the city's own): the four women holding the armillary sphere, Frémiet's eight sea-horses and the turtles, the basin's kerb. +z north up the Jardin Marco-Polo.

name: Palais d'Iéna
note: Perret's Palais d'Iéna (the CESE). Placed on OSM way 79657345's box turned to the rotunda's axis (osmium, 2026-10-29), the rotunda (−z) to the Place d'Iéna, bearing 34.4; OSM's plan extruded flat-roofed in the warm concrete, Perret's swelling, capital-less columns every 4.4 m round every street face under the deep cornice.

name: Palais-Royal — the Conseil d'État and the Cour d'honneur
note: The Salle Richelieu (the Comédie-Française) on the Place Colette and the Rue de Richelieu is drawn too, at the relation's south-west corner. The palace round its two courts (OSM relation 3300400 and its two parts, replaced; it was dressed by paris.json's 'Palais-Royal — galleries' restyle, which still dresses the garden's ranges). Placed on the relation's box turned 19.5° to its axes (osmium, 2026-10-29), front (−z) to the Place du Palais-Royal, bearing 199.5: the wings' frontispieces on the place, the Cour de l'Horloge's colonnade between its grilled arcades, the clock pavilion; the Cour d'honneur arcaded round Buren's columns (burenColumns, paris.json — the court floor is left to it), Contant d'Ivry's front; the Galerie d'Orléans' two low colonnades toward the garden.

name: Moulin Rouge
note: Placed on the box of OSM ways 77806977 and 77807519 and relation 1528981 turned 22° (osmium, 2026-10-30), front (−z) to the Boulevard de Clichy, bearing 202. The low front, the hall behind it, the entrance's two houses are replaced; the mill, the hood, the band and the kiosk are from photographs from the boulevard. The band and hood stand 2 m over the pavement, as they do.

name: La Canopée — Forum des Halles
note: Plan from OSM (osmium, 2026-10-30): the roof way 630511331 and the two wings 630213860 and 630222417, boxed turned 19°, −z to the Rue Berger, bearing 199. The rider sees what the owner's street view shows: a gold glass roof on curved ribs floating clear of two separate long buildings with gold fins over a shop floor, and between them a well with a glass balustrade, escalators and white wayfinding poles. The roof's section (10.7 m at the streets, 14 on the garden, a 15.4 m ridge, 11.2 m over the void) is an estimate from the owner's "about 14 m" and their photograph, not a survey. The city's ground cannot be dug: the well goes only as deep as the IGN lidar's dip (tools/ign-lidar.ts: 3.3 m at the garden end, its returns stop under the roof), and is painted where the ground is flat; the Place Basse's real depth is not modelled. The drawing stands on the streets' grade (fit.groundAt).

name: Maison de la Radio
note: Placed on OSM relation 1255782's box turned so the tower's walls are square to it (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Seine, bearing 132.65. The relation and all its building:parts are replaced by a drawing of the same plans at the same heights.

name: Le Grand Rex
note: Placed on OSM way 54901181's box turned to the boulevard (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Boulevard Poissonnière, bearing 13.7; the corner tower faces the crossing with the Rue Poissonnière. OSM has no height: tower cap 26, lantern 40, letters 44 m read off photographs from the crossing.

name: L'Olympia
note: The 8 m front at 28 Boulevard des Capucines, on OSM way 205926201's box turned 15° (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the boulevard, bearing 165. The canopy stands 2.7 m out over the pavement, as it does. Only the front is drawn: the hall behind is inside the block (the neighbouring ways stay the city's).

name: Théâtre des Champs-Élysées
note: Placed on OSM way 69486335's box turned to the avenue (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Avenue Montaigne, bearing 142.4. Perret's flat marble pavilion, Bourdelle's frieze, the gilt windows and the corner drum from photographs from the avenue; the mass behind the pavilion is a guess at 24 and 32 m.

name: Le Bon Marché
note: Placed on OSM relation 10166422's box turned to its Rue de Sèvres front (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 148.6. Both of the relation's rings are drawn: the main store and the annex west of it. Heights from photographs from the street; the corners are drawn round, as they are, on OSM's sharper plan.

name: Folies Bergère
note: Placed on OSM way 69220738's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue Richer, south. OSM has no name on the way: identified from the street number and the width of the front in photographs. Pico's front, the gilded relief as its rhythm rather than its drawing.

name: Le Bataclan
note: Placed on OSM way 63648846's box turned to the boulevard (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Boulevard Voltaire, bearing 41.6. The painted storey and the old pagoda's tiers from photographs from the boulevard; the café on the left, the entrance on the right.

name: La Cigale
note: Placed on OSM way 77807777's box turned to the boulevard (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Boulevard de Rochechouart, bearing 162.5. Starck's white wave with its portholes and banner, the tower of bows on its right, from photographs from the boulevard.

name: Au Lapin Agile
note: Placed on OSM way 316800538's box turned 11° (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue Saint-Vincent, bearing 11, +x to the Rue des Saules. The pink house, white gable, zinc room, fence and pier from photographs from the crossing; which part of the plan is which is a reading of them.

name: Hôtel Lutetia
note: Placed on OSM way 63454000's box turned to the Boulevard Raspail (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 259.4. The round corner on the crossing with its LVTETIA pediment, the billowing dormers, the awnings from photographs from the crossing; the plan's courts to the north are kept as its outline.

name: Le Louxor
note: Placed on OSM way 63198697's box turned to its corner (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Barbès crossing, bearing 297. The neo-Egyptian corner, canopy, frieze and crown from photographs from the crossing. The way also has a generic parisCivic entry in civic.json until that file is regenerated (tools/paris-civic.ts skips any way another manifest claims).

name: Bourse du Travail
note: Placed on OSM way 63201555's box turned to its street (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue du Château-d'Eau, bearing 38.8. Bouvard's front from photographs from the street; way 1448693889 is the octagonal great hall inside, roofed over here.

name: Marché Saint-Germain
note: Placed on OSM way 22618451's box turned to its street (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue Clément, bearing 356. The arcade, the stepped-back storey, the tile roof and the name over the middle arches from photographs from the street (Commons); heights scaled off them. Arch counts are the bays' rhythm read off those photographs, not a survey.

name: Carreau du Temple
note: Placed on OSM way 30612670's box turned to its street (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue Eugène Spuller, bearing 308. The iron gables, frames and flank from Commons "Carreau du Temple, Paris 9 April 2014", which shows three gables in line and a flank of great arches; that those gables are the ones on the Rue Eugène Spuller is a reading of the photograph against OSM's plan, not a survey. The way also has a generic parisCivic entry in civic.json until that file is regenerated (tools/paris-civic.ts skips any way another manifest claims).

name: Halle Freyssinet
note: Station F. Placed on OSM way 540442288's box along its length (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue Eugène Freyssinet, bearing 239. The section, small arc, great arc, great arc, small arc across the 72 m, from Commons "Halle Freyssinet, Paris 13e" and "Halle Freyssinet - Station F - Outside"; heights and bay scaled off those. Which end carries the STATION F letters is unconfirmed.

name: Palais de la Porte Dorée
note: Placed on OSM way 62819702's box turned to its front (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Avenue Daumesnil, bearing 208 (the entrance bay stands forward on that side of the plan, and the street lies there). The peristyle, the steps and the door from Commons "Palais Porte Doree Facade droite"; Janniot's relief drawn as a texture of carved shapes, not its figures. The way also has a generic parisCivic entry in civic.json until that file is regenerated (tools/paris-civic.ts skips any way another manifest claims).

name: Palais de la Femme
note: Placed on OSM way 63638302's box turned to its street (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue de Charonne, bearing 340; the cut corner on the Rue Faidherbe at +x −z. Meulière, yellow brick, arches, pavilions and wide roofs from Commons "Palais de la Femme, vu depuis la Rue de Charonne, Paris" and the old postcard "Rue Charonne-Palais de la Femme 5"; the name band over the corner arches is drawn from the postcard and may not read that way today. The way also has a generic parisCivic entry in civic.json until that file is regenerated (tools/paris-civic.ts skips any way another manifest claims).

name: Le BHV Marais
note: Placed on OSM way 29168869's box turned to the Rue de Rivoli (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 200; the rotunda on the Rue du Temple corner, where the outline curves. The dome, the sign round the drum, the glazed bays and the banners from Commons "Bazar Hôtel Ville - Paris IV (FR75) - 2020-09-30 - 3"; heights scaled off that photograph.

name: Poste centrale du Louvre
note: Placed on OSM way 29560121's box turned to the Rue du Louvre (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 290, +z to the slant at the back. OSM's height of 28 m. The arcade, the pier grid and the clock and lantern on the corner of the Rue Étienne-Marcel from Commons "Post office street of Louvre (Paris)" and "Bureau Poste Central Louvre - Paris I (FR75) - 2024-09-22 - 1", the corner cut wider than OSM's to what they show. The other two walls are unchecked.

name: Hôtel des Ventes de Drouot
note: Placed on OSM relation 1085247's box turned to the Rue Drouot (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 98, the Rue Rossini at −x. The ribbed metal bays, the ovals, the banners and the red canopy from Commons "P1030038 Paris IX Rue Drouot", the one photograph used; the Rue Rossini is drawn as the same front on that reading.

name: Palais Cambon — Cour des comptes
note: Placed on OSM relation 542460's box turned to the Rue Cambon (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z bearing 119; its outer ring and courts are the plan. The portal, the tablet, the balcony and the flags from Commons "Cour des comptes Paris entrée", "Cambon" and "Cour des comptes (façade du bâtiment sur la rue Cambon)"; heights scaled off them. The bay rhythm either side of the frontispiece is approximate.

name: Palais de la découverte
note: The Grand Palais's west wing, a separate OSM way the Grand Palais entry does not claim. Placed on way 188108997's box turned to its avenue (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Avenue Franklin-Roosevelt, bearing 268; its back stands about 4 m from the Grand Palais model's edge, and that model has a low stone stand-in for this wing behind it. The portal, the bronzes, the colonnade and the attic from Commons "Paris 8e - Palais de la découverte - Façade principale 01".

name: Hôtel de Rochechouart
note: The Ministry of Education, 110 Rue de Grenelle. Placed on OSM relation 1020065's box turned to its street (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Rue de Grenelle, bearing 205; the Rue de Bellechasse at +x. The gate and the street range from Commons "Ministère de l'Éducation Nationale - Paris - 1" and "- 2"; the eighteenth-century house behind is not drawn in detail.

name: Grands Moulins
note: Placed on OSM relation 973246's box turned to its long front (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z to the Esplanade Pierre-Vidal-Naquet, bearing 147. The relation also carries the Cour des Grands Moulins, its court, which stays open. The grid of mill windows, the name band and the square tower with its slate dome from one Mapillary view (1098224344799431) from the Rue Marguerite-Duras: the other walls are drawn as that one's rhythm, unchecked, and which face is the front was chosen by length, not by a photograph.

name: Palais de l'Alma
note: Tétaz's Écuries impériales (1861), now the Élysée's annexes, on the Quai Branly. OSM relation 1084225 (the U of annex ranges round the Cour d'honneur and its hemicycle, the west block round the Cour de la Poste, the riding hall's spur) and way 69045411 (the old palace front on the quai) drawn in east/north metres and registered by enframe.ts (osmium, 2026-11-03); the plan matches the owner's 1930s first-floor plan. IGN's lidar and orthophoto are blurred over the site, so heights are the photographs': annexes 3 storeys to 13 m under low zinc, the quai front two storeys and an attic to 13.5 m, slate mansard to 18, chimneys to 20.5; the manège to a 19 m ridge. Annex fronts after the owner's Street View (brick-arched ground-floor windows, white shutters, banded piers, quoins); quai front after the owner's photograph (pediment, carriage gate, flag). See src/render/landmarks/paris/palaces/alma.ts.

name: Russian spiritual centre — Centre Culturel
note: Wilmotte's pale banded blocks beside the Sainte-Trinité cathedral (2016): a white band at each floor, recessed glass between, a planted roof. Fitted to the OSM way; height from its levels/height tag. Builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/palaces/alma.ts.

name: Russian spiritual centre — Centre Paroissial et Auditorium
note: Wilmotte's pale banded blocks beside the Sainte-Trinité cathedral (2016): a white band at each floor, recessed glass between, a planted roof. Fitted to the OSM way; height from its levels/height tag. Builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/palaces/alma.ts.

name: Russian spiritual centre — École Primaire Franco-Russe
note: Wilmotte's pale banded blocks beside the Sainte-Trinité cathedral (2016): a white band at each floor, recessed glass between, a planted roof. Fitted to the OSM way; height from its levels/height tag. Builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/palaces/alma.ts.

name: Palais Galliera
note: Ginain's palace (1878–94), the Musée de la Mode: the garden front (−z, south) with three glazed arches between Corinthian columns, paired at the end bays, the balustrade and vases, empty statue pedestals; the hemicycle colonnade round the court to the north with its gate pavilion, and the straight colonnade wings to x ±38. Plain east/north metres from OSM relation 1191057 and its parts (osmium), heights from IGN lidar MNS (cornice 17, hall ridge 21, colonnades 10–11): palaces/galliera.ts.

name: Square Brignole-Galliera
note: The palace's garden: railings round OSM way 79232732's ring, the gravel oval and axis walk, clipped trees, empty pedestals for the statues' builder. Same frame as the Palais Galliera: palaces/galliera.ts.

name: Château de Versailles
note: OSM relation 1149002 replaced; its box turned to the garden front's axis (bearing 22.75, osmium 2026-11-04), front (−z) to the Place d'Armes, bearing 112.75. Heights from IGN's MNS (docs/landmarks/MODEL-VERSAILLES.md). First slice: the plan round its courts to one cornice, the chapel, the Opéra.

name: Aile des Ministres sud
note: Mansart’s south range on the Cour royale: two storeys of stone under a slate mansard. Fitted to the OSM way; builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/versailles/communs.ts (heights from the literature, lidar not yet sampled).

name: Aile des Ministres nord
note: The north range on the Cour royale, as the south. Fitted to the OSM way; builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/versailles/communs.ts (heights from the literature, lidar not yet sampled).

name: Grand Commun
note: Mansart’s Grand Commun (1684): brick with stone dressings, three storeys and a mansard. Drawn on its OSM plan with its courts (versailles/dependances-plan.ts, registered by enframe.ts); dressing in versailles/communs.ts, heights from the levels tag and the literature, not the lidar.

name: Hôtel des Réservoirs
note: The Réservoirs de l’Opéra (1752): stone, three storeys and a mansard. Fitted to the OSM way; builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/versailles/communs.ts (heights from the literature, lidar not yet sampled).

name: Orangerie de Versailles
note: Mansart’s Orangerie (1686): one vaulted storey of great arched windows under the terrace. Fitted to the OSM way; builder in src/render/landmarks/paris/versailles/communs.ts (heights from the literature, lidar not yet sampled).

name: Grande Écurie
note: Hardouin-Mansart’s Grande Écurie (1679–82) on the Place d’Armes: two storeys of stone, the ground arched, mansards round its courts. Drawn on its OSM plan with its courts (versailles/dependances-plan.ts, registered by enframe.ts); dressing in versailles/communs.ts, heights from the levels tag and the literature, not the lidar.

name: Petite Écurie
note: Hardouin-Mansart’s Petite Écurie (1679–82), the Grande’s twin across the Avenue de Paris. Drawn on its OSM plan with its courts (versailles/dependances-plan.ts, registered by enframe.ts); dressing in versailles/communs.ts, heights from the levels tag and the literature, not the lidar.

name: Écuries de la Reine
note: The old stables of the King, then the Queen (1672), now the Cour d’appel: stone, three storeys and a mansard.
